nodes.title: Classification of Solids
points: Crystalline Solids: Definite geometric shape, sharp melting point, long-range order, anisotropic (properties like refractive index vary with direction).

Amorphous Solids: Irregular shape, melt over a temperature range, short-range order, isotropic (identical properties in all directions). Pseudo-solids or supercooled liquids (e.g., glass, rubber, plastics).
Types of Crystalline Solids:
1. Molecular: Held by London forces (Ar, CH₄), dipole-dipole (HCl, SO₂), or H-bonds (H₂O ice). Soft, low mp, insulators.
2. Ionic: Held by electrostatic forces (NaCl, ZnS, KNO₃). Hard, brittle, high mp, insulators in solid state but conduct in molten/aqueous state.
3. Metallic: Positive metal ions in a sea of delocalized electrons (Cu, Fe, Ag). High electrical/thermal conductivity, malleable, ductile.

4. Covalent / Network: Giant molecules held by covalent bonds (Diamond, Quartz, Graphite). Very hard, extremely high mp, insulators (except Graphite which is a good conductor due to free electrons between layers).

formulas.label: Anisotropy
formulas.expr: Velocity of light / Refractive index varies with direction in crystalline solids

formulas.label: Graphite conduction
formulas.expr: sp² hybridized carbon with delocalized mobile π-electrons

nodes.title: Crystal Lattice & Unit Cell Types
points: Space Lattice: Regular 3D arrangement of constituent particles (atoms, ions, molecules) in space.
Unit Cell: Smallest repeating structural unit of a crystalline solid that generates the entire crystal lattice.
Four Types of Unit Cells:
1. Simple / Primitive (SCC): Particles present ONLY at the 8 corners.
2. Body-Centred (BCC): Particles at 8 corners + 1 particle at the body centre.
3. Face-Centred (FCC / CCP): Particles at 8 corners + 1 particle at the centre of each of the 6 faces.
4. End-Centred (ECC): Particles at 8 corners + particles at centres of any two opposite faces.
Seven Crystal Systems (Cubic, Tetragonal, Orthorhombic, Hexagonal, Rhombohedral, Monoclinic, Triclinic) yield 14 Bravais Lattices.

nodes.title: Number of Particles (Z) & Coordination Number
points: Simple Cubic (SCC): Z = 8 × (1/8) = 1 atom per unit cell. Coordination Number (CN) = 6.
Body-Centred Cubic (BCC): Z = [8 × (1/8)] + [1 × 1] = 2 atoms per unit cell. CN = 8.
Face-Centred Cubic (FCC / CCP): Z = [8 × (1/8)] + [6 × (1/2)] = 1 + 3 = 4 atoms per unit cell. CN = 12.
Hexagonal Close-Packed (HCP): CN = 12, Z = 6 particles per unit cell.
Coordination Number: Number of nearest neighboring particles touching a given particle.

nodes.title: Edge Length (a) and Particle Radius (r) Relations
points: Simple Cubic (SCC): Particles touch along the cube edge: a = 2r ⟹ r = a / 2 = 0.5 a.
Body-Centred Cubic (BCC): Particles touch along the body diagonal (√3 a = 4r): r = (√3 / 4) a ≈ 0.433 a.
Face-Centred Cubic (FCC): Particles touch along the face diagonal (√2 a = 4r): r = (√2 / 4) a = a / (2√2) ≈ 0.3535 a.
Nearest Neighbor Distance (d = 2r):
SCC: d = a; BCC: d = (√3 / 2) a; FCC: d = a / √2.

nodes.title: Packing Efficiency & Interstitial Voids
points: Packing Efficiency = (Total volume occupied by particles / Total volume of unit cell a³) × 100%.
1. Simple Cubic (SCC): Packing Efficiency = (π/6) × 100% = 52.36% (Void space = 47.64%).
2. Body-Centred Cubic (BCC): Packing Efficiency = (√3 π / 8) × 100% = 68% (Void space = 32%).
3. Face-Centred Cubic (FCC / CCP / HCP): Packing Efficiency = (π / 3√2) × 100% = 74% (Void space = 26%).
Interstitial Voids: If number of close-packed particles = N:
Octahedral Voids (OV) = N; Tetrahedral Voids (TV) = 2N. Total voids = 3N.

nodes.title: Density of Unit Cell & Molar Mass Calculations
points: Density of unit cell: ρ = (Mass of unit cell) / (Volume of unit cell) = (Z · M) / (a³ · N_A).
Where: Z = number of atoms, M = molar mass (g/mol), a = edge length in cm, N_A = Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹).
Unit conversion trick: 1 pm = 10⁻¹⁰ cm; 1 Å = 10⁻⁸ cm; 1 nm = 10⁻⁷ cm.
Number of unit cells in x grams: N_cells = x / (ρ · a³) = (x · N_A) / (Z · M).
Number of atoms in x grams: N_atoms = (x · N_A) / M.

formulas.label: Number of unit cells in mass x
Number of atoms in mass x

nodes.title: Point Defects in Solids
points: Stoichiometric Defects (Ratio of cations to anions remains unchanged):
1. Vacancy Defect: An atom is missing from its normal lattice site. Density DECREASES.
2. Interstitial Defect: An extra atom occupies an interstitial site. Density INCREASES.
3. Schottky Defect: Equal number of cations and anions are missing from lattice sites. High coordination number and similar cation/anion size (NaCl, KCl, CsCl, AgBr). Density DECREASES.

4. Frenkel Defect: Smaller ion (usually cation) is dislocated from its lattice site to an interstitial site. Low coordination number and large difference in ionic radii (ZnS, AgCl, AgBr, AgI). Density REMAINS UNCHANGED.
Special Fact: AgBr exhibits BOTH Schottky and Frenkel defects!
Non-Stoichiometric Defects: Metal Excess (F-centres produce yellow color in NaCl, lilac in KCl, pink in LiCl) and Metal Deficiency (Fe₀.₉₅O).

formulas.label: F-Centre
formulas.expr: Anionic vacancy occupied by an unpaired electron (causes color)

nodes.title: Electrical & Magnetic Properties of Solids
points: Electrical Conductivity: Conductors (10⁴ to 10⁷ S m⁻¹), Insulators (10⁻²⁰ to 10⁻¹⁰ S m⁻¹), Semiconductors (10⁻⁶ to 10⁴ S m⁻¹).

Extrinsic Semiconductors: (1) n-type: Silicon/Germanium (Group 14) doped with Pentavalent atom (P, As, Sb). Conduction via extra electrons; (2) p-type: Group 14 doped with Trivalent atom (B, Al, Ga). Conduction via electron vacancies (holes).
Magnetic Properties:
1. Diamagnetic: All electrons paired, weakly repelled by magnetic field (H₂O, NaCl, C₆H₆).
2. Paramagnetic: Unpaired electrons present, weakly attracted by magnetic field, lose magnetism when field is removed (O₂, Cu²⁺, Fe³⁺).
3. Ferromagnetic: Permanent alignment of magnetic domains in field direction; strongly attracted and retain permanent magnetism (Fe, Co, Ni, CrO₂).

formulas.label: n-type doping
formulas.expr: Group 14 (Si) + Group 15 (P, As) ⟶ Extra free electron

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Distinctions
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive expression for the density of a cubic unit cell: ρ = (Z · M) / (a³ · N_A).
Board Favourite #2: Derive packing efficiency in Body-Centred Cubic (BCC = 68%) and Face-Centred Cubic (FCC = 74%) lattices.
Board Favourite #3: Distinguish between Crystalline solids and Amorphous solids (4 key points: shape, melting point, cleavage, anisotropy).
Board Favourite #4: Distinguish between Schottky defect and Frenkel defect (4 points: mechanism, ionic size condition, density effect, examples).
Board Favourite #5: What are F-centres? Explain why NaCl turns yellow when heated in sodium vapor.

formulas.label: Density derivation
formulas.expr: ρ = Mass / Volume = (Z × m) / a³ = (Z × M) / (a³ × N_A)

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Formula Hacks & Traps
points: Ratio of Radii Shortcut: r_SCC : r_BCC : r_FCC = (a/2) : (√3 a / 4) : (a / 2√2) ≈ 0.500 a : 0.433 a : 0.353 a.
Packing Efficiency Order: FCC (74%) > BCC (68%) > SCC (52.4%). Void space: SCC (47.6%) > BCC (32%) > FCC (26%).
Compound Formula from Voids Trick: If element B forms CCP lattice (N atoms) and A occupies tetrahedral voids: formula is A₂B. If A occupies half the tetrahedral voids: formula is AB.
Schottky vs Frenkel Trap: Schottky lowers density; Frenkel does NOT change density. AgBr shows BOTH Schottky and Frenkel defects!
Unit Conversion Trap: When edge length a is in pm, a(cm) = a × 10⁻¹⁰ cm. (a in cm)³ = a³ × 10⁻³⁰ cm³.

formulas.label: Void stoichiometry shortcut
formulas.expr: N particles ⟹ N octahedral + 2N tetrahedral voids
